source.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion: A Japanese Case Study

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream Japanese G2P performance across model sizes, a different outcome and method from measuring pretraining loss or fitting the original scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports kana CER, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. Its model-size comparisons bear on V6; they do not test power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or the other versions. The TTS comparisons, model citations, and prompting instructions are not results testing those versions.
record.test_reason: It reports downstream Japanese G2P kana CER across size variants within model families, and the authors frame this as the scaling law holding for this task. That is a result on V6 in a new setting. There is no pretraining loss, no fitted curve and no controlled training runs, so it does not bear on V1–V5 or V7. T3 fits better than T2: the study is a new-task benchmark, not a different method aimed at the original question.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say larger models consistently achieved lower CER within a family, and that this shows the scaling law [Kaplan] also holds for G2P, with CER falling monotonically with size. They list size as one key factor alongside version, Japanese-specialized training and prompting mode. The monotonicity claim is made for local LLMs in Fig. 3 and illustrated with only three families.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream kana CER across existing model variants, rather than held-out pretraining loss across controlled training runs; no scaling-law curve is fitted.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model family and version, parse versus direct mode, Japanese-specialized continual pretraining, and reasoning mode.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to CER on one Japanese G2P benchmark and three reported model-family size sweeps; no uncertainty estimates or fitted scaling curve are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other model CER results in Table 1 were not extracted because the paper does not present them as within-family model-size sweeps bearing on V6. TTS comparisons and conventional-tool results do not measure the size-related downstream performance claim.

untested.parts: Predictability: no curve is fitted, no forecast is made and no link to pretraining loss is shown. Size is confounded with training tokens and data across off-the-shelf variants. Only one task and language are covered.
Held-out pretraining loss vs. parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small to large runs.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count.

missing.what: Qwen3 dense family sweep, parse mode: 4B 35.77, 8B 28.13, 14B 17.13, 32B 17.07 (plateau at the top)
Qwen3.5 MoE/API extensions, parse mode: 35B-A3B 6.12, 122B-A10B 7.57, 397B 1.96 (not monotonic in total parameters)
Other within-family size pairs, parse mode: GLM4 9B 26.89→32B 16.82; gpt-oss 20b 7.95→120b 3.03
Direct-mode CER for the same family sweeps, e.g. Gemma3 56.69→28.77→15.16; Qwen3 4B 57.72, 8B 100.15, 14B 32.11, 32B 32.46 (non-monotonic)

record.verdict_notes: The rows' values check against Table 1. Baselines could be stated as the smaller sibling in each family. The record's limits_scope reason (no fitted curves, one task) describes untested parts, not a qualifying result; I replaced it with a limits_scope based on the plateau and non-monotonic cases in Table 1. Model sizes are off-the-shelf releases differing in data and tokens, so size is not isolated. There are no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No fitting on smaller runs or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token growth trends.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No tests of the same power-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests only Japanese G2P CER and selected model-family size comparisons; does not test other downstream tasks or prediction from pretraining loss.
No analysis of fit choices, exponent dependence, or bending of fitted power-law curves.
